item.title: Maresca praises Arsenal but hopes Man City can match champions
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca gestures during the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Manchester City and Napoli at the Etihad Stadium. (is associated with: «Maresca praises Arsenal but hopes Man City can match champions») Mike Egerton/PA Wire/dpa Enzo Maresca accepts Manchester City are some way behind Arsenal in their development - but is determined to match the champions this weekend. City, who travel to the Emirates Stadium on Sunday, have fallen six points behind the Gunners at the top of the Premier League after failing to win their last four matches. It is an abrupt downturn in form after City opened their campaign with seven successive victories, but Maresca believes their relative lack of experience together helps explain their recent difficulties. The City manager, who succeeded Pep Guardiola in the summer, said: “They won the Premier League, played the Champions League final, so that shows how good they are in this moment. “We’re going to try our best to win the game but no doubt in this moment, because they won the Premier League, they are the best. “For two-and-a-half months we were top of the league. Now we are not there and everyone is comparing. That is correct but, for me, it is seven years together against four months together. You cannot compare. “We already showed [our strength] this season in winning important games away – at Old Trafford and Anfield, two important away games. “Sunday is another important one, we showed already and we can win again.” Maresca says he has been happy enough with his side’s general play, but their failure to convert chances and occasional defensive lapses are proving costly. He said: “The problem for us has been [the difference] between what we create and what we concede. “We need to try to be solid, don’t concede, and with the quality that we have, and the amount of chances that we create every game, for sure we need to be more clinical and score more goals. “We need to win duels, second balls and show personality, but this is a nice game for us to see where we are in term of personality and to try to understand the situation more.” City can ill afford to lose if they are to keep pace with the Gunners but Maresca is more concerned about the bigger picture than the immediate ramifications for the title race. He said: “Because we won seven or eight games in a row at the beginning the transition looks more easy, but it is a transition. “Where we can be on Sunday night if we win or draw is important, 100%, but for us it’s a long season and we will see where are in February or March and from there you can set the goals. “Now it’s useless to speak about a target or where we can be at the end of the season.”

item.title: In defence of Red Bull and its footballing exploits
item.description: In defence of Red Bull and its footballing exploits As the Bundesliga’s most controversial member, Die Roten Bullen continue to operate effectively in a hostile environment. Measuring success strictly through silverware is a difficult task, but combing through historic transfer business – in some cases via picturesque Salzburg – tells a rather specific tale. Defined by exits more so than arrivals, the club appears to provide a platform for talent while consistently living up to the brand’s familiar slogan. Dayot Upamecano, arguably the most adept central defender at this moment in time, departed for Bavaria after four seasons in Leipzig. Joshua Kimmich plied his trade there, firstly in 3. Liga and 2. Bundesliga before eventually coming of age in Bayern colours. One other Munich-based player, the plucky and tenacious Konrad Laimer, spent six campaigns in that divisive shirt prior to his free transfer. It has to be said that this is the tip of one very profitable iceberg. Just this summer, the notable sale of Yan Diomande to José Mourinho’s star-studded Real Madrid brought in approximately €125 million alone. Combining last year’s fees for Benjamin Šeško and Xavi Simons, both to the Premier League, equals a similar amount. Factoring in the previous departures of Joško Gvardiol, Dominik Szoboszlai and Christopher Nkunku during a single window also amounts to an eye-watering figure. Credit is due on the recruitment side, of course. However, one important question remains: is it all down to coincidence, or an intense top-down philosophy that allows and actively encourages individuals to showcase their true potential? Extending from Austria to places such as Bragantino and New York, the network Red Bull controls is truly global – one might say a world away from the state of Saxony. In relation to fan ownership and a deeply ingrained ‘50+1’ culture, it may come across as cold or overly commercial. Compare it to some of the financial nightmares at clubs in England and their model suddenly seems rational, progressive and sustainable. Naturally, a willingness to bypass the system that many regard to be the spirit of German football left a lasting impression. Supporters with a deep, long-standing connection to what was once SSV Markranstädt will no doubt feel pangs of betrayal. Also, the same could easily be said for Die Mozartstädter or lovers of ‘soccer’ in the Big Apple. While yet to claim a domestic crown, Leipzig have made serious progress in other areas. Lifting the DFB-Pokal consecutively is no mean feat, especially when you consider the fact that Bayern Munich only returned to Berlin last season for the first time in just over half a decade. Competing in Europe on a regular basis brings elites to Red Bull Arena and sees the side visit historic stadiums, even under that adjusted crest. item.title: George Russell says Lewis Hamilton offers a different example from Max Verstappen
item.description: Motorsport photo In an exclusive Sky Sports F1 interview with Martin Brundle - previewed Friday ahead of its full broadcast before Sunday’s Qatar Grand Prix - George Russell addressed his reignited Las Vegas feud with the four-time world champion Max Verstappen by drawing a quiet, unmistakable contrast between two of Formula 1’s modern giants. "He [Verstappen] is a ruthless competitor, and I massively respect that, but there's also Lewis Hamilton, who I've spent three years team-mates with and watched my whole life," Russell said. "And obviously Toto [Wolff, Mercedes' team principal] spent 12 years with [Hamilton], who is equally a ruthless competitor and absolute animal behind the wheel, but obviously has incredible values and grace and dignity. "And Lewis is somebody who I really look up to and who is an incredible role model for young kids coming through. But there is no right or wrong; there's just opinions. Everyone has different opinions, and some people like driver A and some people like driver B, and as I've grown older, I don't really let it affect me as much." Why the Hamilton benchmark carries real weight The comparison hits harder because Russell lived it firsthand. Across 68 shared starts as Mercedes team-mates from 2022 through 2024, Russell and Hamilton fought on razor-thin margins: deadlocked 34–34 in race finishes, separated by just two total points (697 to 695 in Hamilton’s favour), with Russell holding a 39–29 edge in qualifying. Even when tensions briefly flared on track - such as their opening-lap tangle at Losail in 2023 - the pairing never descended into public character attacks. Verstappen’s Las Vegas response last weekend could hardly have been more different. After Russell called out Verstappen’s driving following their Turn 14 final-practice brush - an incident that earned the Red Bull driver a formal FIA warning for erratic driving - Verstappen won Saturday night’s race while Russell locked up late and clipped the Turn 5 barrier battling team-mate Kimi Antonelli, falling to ninth. item.title: Xabi Alonso admits Chelsea are low on confidence after third straight defeat at Nottingham Forest
item.description: Xabi Alonso admits Chelsea are low on confidence after third straight defeat at Nottingham Forest Xabi Alonso has admitted that Chelsea are low on confidence after losing 3-2 at Nottingham Forest. Chelsea lost a third consecutive game at the City Ground on Friday night as the club's poor run of form continued. Igor Jesus volleyed Forest ahead inside five minutes, before Morgan Gibbs-White doubled the lead from the penalty spot early in the second half, after Wesley Fofana brought down former Chelsea forward Liam Delap in the area. Emmanuel Emegha pulled one back for the Blues, but a second from Gibbs-White restored Forest's advantage. Emegha was on target again, heading home from Cole Palmer's cross, but Chelsea were unable to find an equaliser. Defeat increases the pressure on Alonso, whose side have now conceded 23 goals in just 12 league games. Only Crystal Palace have conceded more in the Premier League , ahead of the weekend's fixtures. Chelsea are eighth in the Premier League table, five points adrift of the Champions League places, having played a game more than fourth-placed Liverpool. Alonso urges Chelsea to find solutions after Forest defeat extends losing streak to three games Reflecting on the result, Alonso said his side are suffering from a crisis of confidence. "Many things didn’t go the way we wanted," the Spaniard said in his post-match interview. "I think we are low in confidence; you see that the team is struggling to hold a result. After getting [a goal back for] the 2-1, we then conceded the 3-1 just when we had a little bit of boost from the goal. "We can do better for sure. At this level, you need to hold results and you don’t have to concede that much. That is why we are losing the last games. "So, everything is not going our way. We are responsible for that, and we are responsible for trying to find solutions."

item.title: Gaza’s chess players survive a genocide and rebuild a community
item.description: Gaza City – Raghad Rabie, 18, never expected to beat her chess coach, Raghad Adas, at chess. During the friendly match, Rabie deliberately left some of her pieces exposed to distract her opponent as she planned a move that would deliver a checkmate in two turns. Her strategy worked, giving her confidence in her abilities as a chess player. But the match also reflected something bigger: The return of chess to Gaza after the Israeli genocide devastated sporting activities across the enclave. Rabie began learning chess in August 2025, when she was displaced in southern Gaza. Looking for something new to learn and a way to occupy her time, she taught herself the basic rules online before joining a training course run by Adas. “I had admired chess players for a long time and wanted to learn the game. I started on my own, then the course helped me improve,” she says. She has since participated in two tournaments and dreams of becoming a chess grandmaster, the goal of every serious chess player, and representing Palestine internationally. But pursuing that ambition in Gaza, still under an Israeli siege and subject to daily air attacks despite an October 2025 “ceasefire”, is difficult. There is no permanent training venue for chess players, so weekly gatherings take place in different locations, including the Lord Cafe in the al-Rimal neighbourhood of Gaza City. Raghad Rabie, 18, one of the chess players at Stalemate [Lina Abu Zayed/Al Jazeera] To become an International Chess Federation (FIDE)-rated grandmaster, as Rabie hopes, requires thousands of hours of dedicated practice and study. But a shortage of chessboards, clocks and chess books – and soaring prices for any available chess equipment – has made this mission difficult. Before the war, Adas was captain of the girls’ Spark team, playing in Palestinian Chess Federation tournaments. She was also among 10 players selected to take part in matches against other Palestinians from the occupied West Bank with the goal of forming a national team, which it was hoped would compete internationally. Travel arrangements and permit procedures had been completed, but then Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza broke out in October 2023, killing at least 74,000 Palestinians and laying waste to the Palestinian enclave. “I was excited about taking part in an international tournament, but the war made everything much more difficult,” Adas told Al Jazeera. Adas said the team’s headquarters was destroyed, its players were scattered across Gaza, and she lost contact with several former teammates amid the forced Israeli displacements. About a year after the war began, Adas started teaching chess in shelters, initially volunteering before working with organisations and eventually continuing her mission independently. She noticed a growing interest in the sport among newcomers, as well as the return of players who had stopped playing during the genocide. item.title: Lakers are ‘real’ deal — even Victor Wembanyama thinks so
item.description: Like the rest of us, Victor Wembanyama was skeptical of the Lakers. The darlings of the NBA entered Friday’s game against the Spurs with the top record in the NBA at 15-3. But they hadn’t played the league’s most elite teams. They hadn’t really proven themselves. So, Friday was a temperature check. It was a harsh dressing room mirror that would expose their flaws in front of a national television audience. How did they do? “As a team I wasn’t sure what they were built of, at least from the start of the season,” Wembanyama acknowledged. “But it’s real.” The Lakers lost, 99-96 . But the final score was far less important than what transpired. The Lakers led by as much as 20 points. They bottled up Wembanyama in the first half, holding him to just eight points on nine shot attempts and five rebounds. Over that period, Luka Dončić had as many rebounds as Wembanyama (five) while scoring more than twice as many points (19). It was incredible. The Spurs reached the Finals last year. Wembanyama is unequivocally considered the next face of the league once the 41-year-old LeBron James retires. This was about as big of a test as the Lakers could get. And at the beginning of the game, they were jaw-droppingly good. Then things fell apart. The Lakers were outscored in the third quarter, 30-14. Over that period, they were outshot from the field, 48.1% to 25%, and from beyond the 3-point line, 37.5% to 15.4%. They unraveled, culminating in Keldon Johnson making a 3-pointer with 1.8 seconds left to knot the score at 68-68 heading into the fourth quarter. The next 12 minutes were a dogfight. Both teams wanted this. Victor Wembanyama (left) and Luka Dončić look on during the Lakers’ 99-96 NBA Cup loss to the Spurs on Nov. 27, 2026, in San Antonio. NBAE via Getty Images Wembanyama and Dončić, who are in a two-horse race for the MVP Award , knew the stakes. Everyone on the court was acutely aware of the chatter this game would generate. They knew this contest meant so much more than another regular-season game in November. Ultimately, the Spurs clawed a few inches ahead as the final buzzer sounded. After Wembanyama’s sluggish start, he finished with 25 points, 16 rebounds, four steals and two blocked shots. But he had as many field-goal attempts (25) as points. Dončić had a game-high 31 points, six rebounds, eight assists and three steals. But he went 1-for-13 from beyond the arc. Luka Dončić looks to make a move on De’Aaron Fox during the Lakers’ NBA Cup road loss to the Spurs. AP Photo/Darren Abate Both of them shined. Both of them struggled. The Spurs likely prevailed because they’ve experienced moments like this before. They were three wins away from a championship last year. If they hadn’t blown double-digit leads in all five of their games against the Knicks in the Finals, they would’ve been the reigning champions. item.title: Roma continue talks with Endrick’s entourage
item.description: Roma continue talks with Endrick’s entourage Roma has no intention of abandoning the pursuit of Endrick, despite José Mourinho’s position continuing to complicate a possible January move. Fabrizio Romano took to his YouTube channel to discuss the Brazilian striker’s future, confirming the Giallorossi’s contact with his team: “Roma have been calling for weeks, and I’m sure they will continue to do so.” The journalist explained that AC Milan also remains strongly interested in the 2006-born player, so much so that they initiated initial contact in August to try to position themselves for the upcoming transfer window. The Rossoneri continue to monitor the player, even in the summer, should the conditions for a January move not be met. Roma remains among the clubs interested, waiting to see if Real Madrid will change their position. The main obstacle remains Mourinho, who has publicly reiterated his desire to retain Endrick. This stance could prevent the Brazilian’s departure during the winter transfer window, although the coach himself has acknowledged that the final decision will rest with Real Madrid’s management. As Fabrizio Romano himself reported, Liverpool and Aston Villa also attempted to acquire the Brazilian over the summer, but both received negative responses from Real Madrid.

item.title: Red Sox Floated as Landing Spot for Former Yankees Two-Time All-Star
item.description: Red Sox Floated as Landing Spot for Former Yankees Two-Time All-Star originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Red Sox continue to see multiple free agents leave the board, including ones who can help them on both sides of the baseball. However, the Red Sox have also made some impressive moves this offseason, so they should feel pretty confident about what they've done so far. As the Red Sox look for ways to improve, doing so on the mound will be at the top of the priority list. After losing Sonny Gray to the Minnesota Twins, the Red Sox have an opportunity to land another right-hander who could come in and help. One interesting target is Clay Holmes, who has played for the New York Mets and New York Yankees, among other teams. “Yet another pitcher who was traded during the ‘26 season, Holmes made nine starts for both the Mets (2.39 ERA) and Cubs (4.25 ERA). After suffering a fractured right fibula on May 15 when he was struck by a comebacker against the Yankees, Holmes proved to be healthy when he returned. “His experiences in New York (Yankees and Mets) could set Holmes up well for a stint with the Red Sox. In ‘25, his first season with a significant amount of starts, Holmes proved he was up to the task (12-8, 3.53 ERA) for the Mets,” Ian Browne of MLB.com wrote . Holmes has been a very interesting player throughout his career, as he's proven he can be among the top starters in baseball. However, he's worked out of the bullpen for much of his career. He’s been a full-time starter only since 2025. Since then, he's had some up-and-down moments, but he was really good for the Mets in 2025, posting a 3.53 ERA in 166.2 innings. His strikeout stuff has certainly declined since his time as a reliever, though he never had great strikeout numbers. However, at 33 and likely not too expensive, he could be a decent option to pursue. item.title: Arsenal threaten Barcelona pursuit of 22-year-old Sporting defender – report
item.description: Arsenal threaten Barcelona pursuit of 22-year-old Sporting defender – report Arsenal have emerged as a potential rival to Barcelona in the pursuit of Sporting CP right-back Ivan Fresneda, with Mikel Arteta’s side making contact with the defender’s representatives as they plan for the future of their right flank. According to a report from The Athletic (h/t SPORT ), Arsenal view the 22-year-old Spaniard as a possible long-term successor to Ben White, and it is a development that could complicate Barcelona’s long-standing interest in a player they have followed since his breakthrough at Real Valladolid. Arsenal identify Fresneda as a future option at right back As reported by the outlet, Arsenal are assessing their right-back options as part of their longer-term squad planning. In this regard, Fresneda has attracted attention after establishing himself at Sporting and with the Spanish national team, where his development has gathered momentum following a difficult initial period in Portugal. Arsenal are also interested in signing Ivan Fresneda. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images) The talented full-back has recorded four assists in 16 appearances this season, and his attacking contribution, age and potential to improve further have strengthened his appeal to clubs looking for a long-term defensive option. Arsenal’s interest is not limited to mere scouting, with reports indicating that the Premier League champions have already contacted his representatives, although no agreement or formal transfer bid has been confirmed. Barcelona have followed Fresneda since 2023 Fresneda is a familiar name to Barcelona’s sporting department. The Catalan club seriously considered signing him in the summer of 2023 , when he was still playing for Valladolid and regarded as one of Spain’s promising young full-backs. Barcelona ultimately chose to bring Joao Cancelo back to the club instead, while Fresneda moved to Sporting for a reported fee of around €9 million. His contract in Lisbon runs until June 2028. Barcelona are still keeping an eye on Ivan Fresneda. (Photo by Gualter Fatia/Getty Images) Interest from Barcelona has resurfaced in recent weeks , as reports from Portugal have indicated the Blaugrana are monitoring his progress, with sporting director Deco involved in assessing the defender. Simply put, Barcelona are looking for a long-term solution at right-back after considering other targets, including Pedro Porro. Sporting hold a strong position in the transfer battle Crucially, Fresneda’s improvement has also strengthened Sporting’s position, with the Portuguese club now keen to extend his contract until 2031 and retain an €80 million release clause, making a potential transfer difficult to negotiate. For Barcelona, Arsenal’s contact already poses a big problem, and if the player ultimately signs an extension with the Portuguese club, their pursuit could well and truly rest once and for all.

item.description: Longest scoring streaks in Premier League history Evanilson is enjoying the best goalscoring form of his Bournemouth career, with the Cherries' centre-forward having scored in six consecutive Premier League appearances. The 27-year-old will target a seventh successive game with a goal against Fulham this weekend, an achievement recorded on just 19 occasions in Premier League history. A longer run would put him among an exclusive group of players to have scored in eight or more consecutive appearances. Alexander Isak - Newcastle (8) Alexander Isak scored in eight consecutive games for Newcastle United between December 2024 and January 2025. The Swedish striker began his run with a goal in a 3-3 draw with Liverpool before scoring in wins over Leicester City and Brentford. He subsequently helped the Magpies to six consecutive victories, scoring 11 goals across the eight-game period, including a hat-trick against Ipswich Town. Jamie Vardy - Leicester City (8) No stranger to scoring streaks, Jamie Vardy went eight-in-a-row with a goal during the 2019/20 campaign. Leicester won all eight games across that spell, including a record-equalling 9-0 win away at Southampton that saw Vardy and teammate Ayoze Perez score hat-tricks. The Foxes' forward ended the campaign with 23 league goals to win the Premier League Golden Boot. Daniel Sturridge - Liverpool (8) Daniel Sturridge might be one of the Premier League's modern 'what if?' players. Injuries derailed what was a stunning start to his Liverpool career, as Sturridge scored 31 league goals in 43 games across his first 18 months at Anfield. Sturridge enjoyed a remarkable 2013/14 campaign, scoring in eight consecutive Premier League appearances as Liverpool challenged for the title. The forward struck 21 league goals that season, finishing behind teammate Luis Suarez in the Golden Boot standings. Ruud van Nistelrooy - Manchester United (8) Ruud van Nistelrooy features twice on this list of the longest scoring streaks in Premier League history. His first entry came during his debut season at Manchester United , when the Dutchman scored in eight consecutive league appearances between December 2001 and January 2002. Van Nistelrooy enjoyed a prolific first campaign at Old Trafford, scoring 36 goals in all competitions and earning the PFA Players' Player of the Year award. item.title: Real Madrid superstar leaves a lasting impression on Paul Pogba: ‘What he does is really impressive’
item.description: Real Madrid superstar leaves a lasting impression on Paul Pogba: ‘What he does is really impressive’ Real Madrid have been in excellent form for the past couple of months, with Jose Mourinho’s side securing 10 consecutive victories. One player who has become increasingly influential during this run is Jude Bellingham, with the Englishman returning to his very best. Bellingham had a couple of seasons to forget with Los Blancos as he struggled with shoulder problems and couldn’t replicate the highs of his debut season in Spain. However, the 23-year-old now looks close to his best , scoring goals and providing assists that have proved decisive for his team. The midfielder’s resurgence has received considerable attention, and former Juventus star Paul Pogba has now spoken very highly of him. Pogba makes massive Bellingham admission In an interview, the French World Cup winner was asked to identify a midfielder from the current generation who particularly impressed him. “Midfielder to watch from this generation? Jude Bellingham,” the Frenchman said (h/t Madrid Xtra ). Jude Bellingham is hitting new heights at Real Madrid this season. (Photo by Tullio M. Puglia/Getty Images) Asked whether he saw similarities between their playing styles, Pogba went a step further, admitting that Bellingham has greater ability than he ever did. “I believe that he has way more ability, and he’s from a different generation. What he does on the pitch is really impressive.” Pogba made a name for himself as one of the most technically gifted and physically dominant midfielders in Europe. His exceptional passing range and creativity, along with his long-range shooting, made him one of the most important players for France under Didier Deschamps. Bellingham thriving under Mourinho His comments about Bellingham come at an excellent time, following the Englishman’s second-half heroics against PSV Eindhoven. Bellingham has been in excellent form since the 2026 World Cup. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Having begun the game on the bench, he came on in the second half and scored a spectacular goal to inspire Madrid’s 5-1 Champions League comeback. Beyond his goalscoring ability, Bellingham’s greatest strength lies in his versatility. He can carry the ball through midfield and contribute defensively, making him a complete midfielder. With players like Arda Guler and Bernardo Silva providing creativity around him, Mourinho has the perfect system to get the best out of Jude Bellingham. Just one goal short of matching his tally from the entire previous campaign, Bellingham will be eager to maintain his form in the coming months.

item.title: From England: Roma tracking Federico Chiesa
item.description: From England: Roma tracking Federico Chiesa New confirmation is coming from England regarding the future of Federico Chiesa, one of the wingers linked to Roma ahead of the January transfer window. According to The Athletic , the 1997-born player will leave Liverpool in 2027, either during the winter transfer window or at the end of the season. The former Juventus player is now on the fringes of Andoni Iraola’s coaching project, having only played two minutes of the Premier League match against Manchester City on October 11th since the start of the season. As reported in recent days by Corriere dello Sport, Chiesa has been offered to Roma, with Tony D’Amico working to provide Gasperini with a new attacking winger. Inter, Atalanta, and Lazio are also reportedly interested in the 2021 European champion, while the player is reportedly keen on a return to Juventus. Complicating the former Juventus player’s potential arrival in the capital are Liverpool’s demands, which have so far valued the Italian at around €15 million, along with a salary of €7.5 million per season. Roma, on the other hand, are reportedly keen to strengthen their attack through a loan with an option to buy.

item.title: “Arch is Collapsing”, “The Arch We’ve Got All Season”: Texas Fans Have Had Enough as Arch Manning Struggles Again vs Aggies
item.description: Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning - SEC Football Kickoff Media Day © IMAGN Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning endured another difficult outing in the 16-6 win against Texas A&M. The quarterback struggled offensively in the Lone Star Showdown at Kyle Field on Friday. Coming off an impressive 287-yard, two-touchdown performance against Arkansas, Manning’s pass production was challenged by the Aggies. The Longhorns quarterback completed 18 of 34 passes for 143 yards, one touchdown, and one interception. Manning threw an end-zone interception to Texas A&M defensive back Tawfiq Byard, giving the Aggies a chance at a comeback in the final quarter. Fans reacted to the quarterback’s struggle in the Aggies’ game. “Arch is collapsing. Oh no. This is the Arch we’ve got all season,” one fan wrote. “Man, Arch Manning tries to throw fastballs from 10 yards away. Give credit to this A&M defense, but Arch needs to understand they just need to win the game. My goodness,” one fan added. “He has zero football awareness, geez. Anything but an interception and game over,” one fan commented. “Put in Lacey,” one fan noted. “He gonna be the reason Texas don’t win,” one fan remarked. “I actually hope Jerry drafts him,” one fan joked. Manning’s struggles against LSU raised the question of whether the Longhorns quarterback can deliver against elite opponents. In the narrow 22-21 win against the Tigers, Manning threw three interceptions and completed just 19 of 35 passes for 174 yards. Entering Friday’s matchup against Texas A&M, Manning has completed 208 of 314 passes for 2,485 yards, 21 touchdowns against 10 interceptions. He also has four rushing touchdowns. Arch Manning’s Comparison Downplayed To Texas A&M QB Just ahead of the kickoff at Kyle Field, Arch Manning received a surprising comparison from former Texas A&M defensive back Jordan Pugh during an appearance on TexAgs Live. The All-Big 12 defensive back compared the “average” Texas signal-caller to Aggies quarterback Marcel Reed. “Arch is just as average as Marcel is right now,” Pugh said . The comparison may feel off, as Reed had completed 160 of 287 passes for 1,712 yards this season entering the matchup against the Longhorns. item.title: Winning is the only option for Iraola ahead of first Merseyside derby
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola gestures on the touchline during the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Fenerbahce and Liverpool at Sukru Saracoglu Stadium. (is associated with: «Winning is the only option for Iraola ahead of first Merseyside derby») Adam Davy/PA Wire/dpa Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola heads into his first Merseyside derby knowing there is only one option: win. Just two defeats in the last 34 meetings with Everton mean expectations for the short trip to Hill Dickinson Stadium are high. Most of the statistics associated with England’s most-played derby favour the Reds, looking for a fourth successive victory over their neighbours for the first time since August 1991, as the Toffees have won just one of the last 15 home encounters against Liverpool. As a proud Basque, Iraola knows the significance of local rivalries, but Sunday’s game is on an all together higher level. “I played a lot, also a big derby – Athletic [Bilbao]-Real Sociedad. I think they are special because – the same as here – you have a lot of friends that are from the opposing team, sometimes a member of your family even,” he said. “Definitely it’s a game that lasts longer. It’s not a game you play and, OK, you speak a little bit next week. “No, normally this thing lasts long and the winner reminds the other side normally a lot of time. “I experienced it a lot as a player and this is going to be my first one here, but I can feel everyone wants to win it, yes.” Liverpool’s form is encouraging as they have won their last three in all competitions while Everton go into the game off the back of a 4-0 humbling by Brentford, their first defeat in four matches in all competitions. The two teams were separated by five places and five points heading into the weekend but Iraola will not allow his fourth-placed side to be complacent. “I think it is a derby and derbies are always different. It doesn’t matter where you are in the standings, it doesn’t matter the run that you are in,” he added. Four players – Jeremy Jacquet, Ronald Araujo, Bradley Barcola and Trey Nyoni – look set for their derby debuts. The 21-year-old Jacquet has slotted into the centre of defence to become Virgil van Dijk’s regular partner and has impressed but his composure will be tested in the derby, although Iraola does not believe the occasion will trouble him. “He has this self-confidence. He is also improving with the language and that always helps with communications with team-mates,” he said of the newly capped France international. “He doesn’t have a lot of games or experience, but he is in high-level games and playing with the national team. “Also, he has help from experienced players around him. That helps when you are young, but he is giving back with performances.”

item.title: Baylor Set to Name Multi-Time Conference Champion as Next Head Coach
item.description: DALLAS, TEXAS - DECEMBER 26: Head coach Jeff Traylor of the UTSA Roadrunners reacts during the second quarter F in the 2025 SERVPRO First Responder Bowl at Gerald J. Ford Stadium on December 26, 2025 in Dallas, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) Getty One of the open Power Four coaching jobs is set to be filled, at least that’s according to ESPN’s Pete Thamel as of Friday night. According to Thamel, Baylor is going to hire UTSA head coach Jeff Traylor as the school’s next leader. Baylor Set to Hire UTSA’s Jeff Traylor as Their Next Head Coach With an official announcement expected to take place in the coming days, Traylor will stay in Texas and jump up the Big 12 after posting a 63-28 record in seven seasons with the Roadrunners. He has UTSA at 10-2 and about to play for a conference title in the American Championship Game. Another win and Traylor, 58, would have his highest victory total since 2022, back when his team finished 11-3 after a loss in the Cure Bowl. But no matter how 2026 ends, Traylor has proven to be a consistent winner at the Group of 5 level. Traylor Turned UTSA Into a Championship Program In seven seasons, he owns a career winning clip of .689, has capped off every season with a bowl appearance, has three-straight bowl wins and two conference championships (both when a member of Conference USA). Before joining UTSA ahead of the 2020 campaign, Traylor served as Arkansas’ assistant head coach and running backs coach in 2018 and 2019. He served in the same position at SMU in 2017 and was a social teams coach at the University of Texas in 2015 and 2016. Traylor started his coaching career working up the Texas high school ranks in the late 1990s, eventually landing a head role at Gilmer High School from 2000-2014. And while Traylor may not be a flashy name nationally, he will now be able to test his system and recruiting chops with resources at his disposal. Baylor is Hoping for More Consistent Success Moving Forward Baylor is looking to turn the page to a more successful next chapter after firing Dave Aranda in late October. Aranda was 40-40 overall and 26-32 in conference play in six seasons. Never able to duplicate his second year, when he led the Bears to a 12-2 record, a Big 12 title and a victory in the Sugar Bowl, Aranda was 4-3 in 2026 at the time of his dismissal, a disappointing start to a season that followed going 5-7 in 2025. Aranda only reached a bowl game in three seasons, losing his most recent opportunities in 2022 and 2024. Club scouts have closely monitored Nusa's displays in both the Bundesliga and the Champions League ahead of the winter market. However, any hopes of a straightforward mid-season deal have been complicated by RB Leipzig's firm valuation of their prized asset. Leipzig hold firm on winter exit According to Sky Germany , Leipzig have no desire to part ways with Nusa midway through the campaign. The German club will only entertain a January departure if a suitor tables an 'astronomical offer', defined as a bid surpassing the €100m (£83.5m) threshold. Leipzig's reluctance stems from their own ambitions this season. Sitting fourth in the Bundesliga and still battling for a play-off spot in the Champions League league phase, the club want to retain their strongest squad for the remainder of the term. Nusa's rapid rise in Germany Nusa has justified that lofty valuation with a sensational campaign in Germany. Having arrived at Leipzig from Club Brugge two years ago in a €21m (£17.8m) deal, the forward has become one of the team's standout performers, registering nine goals and eight assists in 17 appearances so far this season. Nusa has already cemented his place as a key figure in Norway's attack, netting ten goals in 36 appearances for his country. What's next for Arsenal? Arsenal now face a decisive call ahead of the January window: test RB Leipzig's resolve with a massive bid or explore alternative attacking targets for Arteta. Leipzig have already proven they are willing to play the long game in the transfer market. item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
